info.title: Collecta PayPal Sandbox
info.description: Collecta lets a collections agent work with the PayPal sandbox: create, send, remind and cancel invoices, create and capture checkout orders, send payouts and list account transactions to reconcile payments.

get.description: Lists the balance transactions of the PayPal account, such as payments received, refunds, fees and payouts, within a date range of at most 31 days. Useful to reconcile payments received against invoices. New transactions can take a few hours to appear.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: The start of the date range as a date and time with seconds and a time zone (Z or an offset such as -07:00), for example 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: The end of the date range as a date and time with seconds and a time zone, for example 2026-01-31T23:59:59Z. At most 31 days after the start date.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: The transaction details to include in the response. Always all, because PayPal returns only the transaction info by default.

parameters.name: transaction_id
parameters.description: Returns only transactions with this PayPal transaction ID, which is 17 characters long (19 for an order ID). Two transactions can share an ID.

parameters.name: transaction_type
parameters.description: Returns only transactions with this PayPal transaction event code, for example T0006 for a checkout payment or T0007 for a website payment.

parameters.name: transaction_amount
parameters.description: Returns only transactions whose gross amount is in this range, written in minor units as LOW TO HIGH. For example 500 TO 1005 finds amounts from 5.00 to 10.05.

parameters.name: transaction_currency
parameters.description: Returns only transactions in this three-character ISO-4217 currency code, for example USD.

parameters.name: balance_affecting_records_only
parameters.description: Y returns only transactions that change the account balance, which is the default. N returns all transactions.

parameters.name: transaction_status
parameters.description: Returns only transactions with this status code: S for success, P for pending, D for denied or V for reversed.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page number to return, starting at 1.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: The number of transactions to return per page, from 1 to 500.

InvoiceNotification.description: Options for the email notification that PayPal sends for the invoice.

send_to_recipient.description: Whether PayPal emails the notification to the customer. Defaults to true. With false, nothing is emailed and the customer payment link of the invoice can be shared through another channel.

send_to_invoicer.description: Whether PayPal also emails a copy of the notification to the invoicer. Defaults to false.

subject.description: The subject of the notification email. PayPal currently ignores a supplied value and always uses its own standard subject.

note.description: A note to the customer. PayPal currently ignores a supplied value and always uses its own standard text.

additional_recipients.description: CC email addresses that receive a copy. Only addresses already listed as additional recipients of the invoice are valid. When empty, all of them are notified.

items.description: An email address that receives a copy of the notification.

InvoiceSearch.description: The criteria used to search invoices. All criteria are optional and are combined with AND.

status.description: The invoice statuses to match. For unpaid or overdue invoices use SENT, UNPAID and PARTIALLY_PAID. PAID_EXTERNAL and MARKED_AS_PAID are invoices paid outside PayPal.

recipient_email.description: The email address of the customer who was billed. Partial values are matched.

invoice_number.description: The invoice number shown to the customer. Partial values are matched.

invoice_date_range.description: Filters invoices by invoice date, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

start.description: The start of the range, for example 2026-01-31. Required when the range is used.

end.description: The end of the range, for example 2026-01-31. Required when the range is used.

due_date_range.description: Filters invoices by payment due date, in YYYY-MM-DD format. A range that ends before today finds overdue invoices.

start.description: The start of the range, for example 2026-01-31. Required when the range is used.

end.description: The end of the range, for example 2026-01-31. Required when the range is used.

payment_date_range.description: Filters invoices by the date and time a payment was received.

start.description: The start of the range, for example 2026-01-31T00:00:00Z. Required when the range is used.

end.description: The end of the range, for example 2026-01-31T00:00:00Z. Required when the range is used.

creation_date_range.description: Filters invoices by the date and time the invoice was created.

start.description: The start of the range, for example 2026-01-31T00:00:00Z. Required when the range is used.

end.description: The end of the range, for example 2026-01-31T00:00:00Z. Required when the range is used.

total_amount_range.description: Filters invoices by total amount. Both the minimum and the maximum are required, in the same currency.

lower_amount.description: The lowest invoice total to match.

currency_code.description: The three-character ISO-4217 currency code, for example USD.

value.description: The amount as a decimal string, for example 150.00.

memo.description: Text in the private bookkeeping memo of the invoice.

archived.description: Whether to return archived invoices (true) or only active invoices (false). Returns both when empty.

intent.description: CAPTURE to collect the payment right after the customer approves, or AUTHORIZE to place a hold and capture later.

invoice_id.description: Your own invoice number for this payment. It appears in the customer's transaction history and emails and in the transaction reports. By default it must be unique within the merchant account, so a second order with the same value is rejected.

custom_id.description: Your own identifier for this payment, such as the CRM record ID. It appears in transaction reports but is not shown to the customer.

reference_id.description: An identifier for the purchase unit. Needed only when the order has several purchase units.

payment_source.description: How the customer pays. Only the PayPal wallet checkout experience is exposed.

paypal.description: Settings for payment with a PayPal account.

experience_context.description: Customizes the PayPal checkout pages shown to the customer.

return_url.description: The web address the customer is redirected to after approving the payment. Supply it whenever the payment link is sent to the customer directly, otherwise PayPal shows an error page after approval.

cancel_url.description: The web address the customer is redirected to after cancelling the payment.

brand_name.description: The business name shown on the PayPal checkout pages instead of the name of the PayPal account.

user_action.description: PAY_NOW shows a Pay Now button and suits a known final amount. CONTINUE shows a Continue button for flows where the amount is confirmed later.

shipping_preference.description: Where the shipping address comes from. NO_SHIPPING hides the shipping address, which suits payments for invoices and services.

payment_method_preference.description: IMMEDIATE_PAYMENT_REQUIRED accepts only instant payment methods, so the captured payment is never left pending. UNRESTRICTED accepts any payment method.

landing_page.description: The first PayPal page shown to the customer: LOGIN, GUEST_CHECKOUT (pay by card without an account), NO_PREFERENCE or BILLING (older name for the card page).

id.description: The PayPal ID of the order. Use it to get or capture the order.

PayPalRequestId.description: A unique ID for this request that makes it safe to retry. Repeating a request with the same ID does not create a duplicate. PayPal keeps the ID for 6 hours.
